newsitem.title: UK: Urals firm, Saharan offered at Dated +45 cts.
newsitem.headline: Urals firm, Saharan offered at Dated +45 cts.

text.p: Urals was discussed at steady to firm levels on Tuesday and a cargo sold late last week between traders was offered out again, traders said.
The Biruinta loading June 27-29 was offered by the trader who bought the cargo late last week but no number was immediately known, they said.
The Biruinta was reportedly sold last week at between Dated Brent -$1.00 and Dated -$1.10.
The Matilda, loading one million barrels of Urals at the end of June, changed hands late on Monday but the value was private and confidential, traders said.

One trader said he understood the agreed value of the Matilda was close to Dated Brent -$1.00, near the top of recent assessments and trades. He said he had heard discussion at this number on Tuesday.

The trader argued support for the Russian sour came from lack of progress in completing preparations for a resumption of exports of Iraqi Kirkuk under the second phase of the U.N. oil for food programme.
But other traders insist refiners would probably only pay around Dated -$1.10/$1.15.

Traders continue to await Syrian state oil company Sytrol's pricing for Syrian Light and Souedie for July. One said it appeared Sytrol was holding back a final decision in order to wait for the Urals market to settle at a higher number.
Some believe Urals will firm in the event that delays occur in preparations for a resumption of exports of Iraq's Kirkuk sour under the second six-month phase of the U.N. "oil-for-food" programme.
